summary: Iteration 2 end-to-end testing complete for Jivdani B2B. Backend: 34/34 pytest passed (25 regression in backend_test.py + 9 new in test_iteration2.py) covering: GET /api/admin/purchase-list aggregation across restaurants & delivered exclusion, default tomorrow, admin-only auth, DELETE /api/orders/{id} (success/404/403), PUT /api/restaurants/{id} name+phone+address+password (login with new password verified). Frontend: Admin Purchase List page correctly aggregated 2.0+1.5=3.5kg for shared veg across 2 restaurants for tomorrow, summary cards show veg count/restaurants/total, Print button present. Admin Orders search filters by restaurant name, delete-order button removes order. Admin Restaurants search filters, edit dialog renames restaurant and persists. Restaurant My Orders (/my-orders) page has working All/Pending/Confirmed/Delivered filter chips and search filters by vegetable name. Regression: place order, confirm with override, mark delivered, ledger, payments still work (confirmed via backend_test.py).

minor.issue: Still uses query parameter instead of JSON body (carried over from iteration 1; works but inconsistent).
Deleting a confirmed/delivered order silently drops billed amount from ledger without an audit trail. Consider soft-delete or refund-style accounting.

(carry-over) Iteration 1 minor still applies: orphan payments after restaurant deletion are now cleaned via cascade in DELETE /api/restaurants, but POST /api/payments still allows over-payment producing negative pending.

issues: DialogContent likely still missing aria-describedby (Radix a11y warning carry-over from iteration 1).
Date input is a native <input type='date'> rather than the shadcn Calendar component used elsewhere; consider replacing for visual consistency.

action_items: Consider switching PUT /api/orders/{id}/status to JSON body for API consistency.
Add aria-describedby/DialogDescription to the Edit Restaurant dialog and other Radix dialogs (iter1 carry-over).
Decide handling for deletion of confirmed/delivered orders: confirm via UI prompt (already present) but consider soft-delete for audit.
Replace native date input in AdminPurchaseList with shadcn Calendar for UX consistency.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py grew further (~696 lines) - still single-file. Recommend splitting (carry-over).

purchase_list aggregation uses set() for restaurants but est_amount sums it.qty*it.rate snapshotted on order creation; if rate changes after order placement, est_amount in purchase list will lag actual rate. Acceptable for the next-morning purchase plan but worth documenting.
DELETE /api/orders/{id} has no role-scoping beyond admin and no foreign-key cleanup (e.g., if any future payments table referenced orders); fine for current schema.

AdminPurchaseList uses tomorrow_str() default on backend but frontend defaults the input to local-tz tomorrow; on tz boundaries this could disagree. Backend timezone is UTC; if testing across DST boundary near midnight IST, date may differ by 1 day. Consider sending explicit date from frontend always.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all 4 flows: purchase-list, order search/delete, restaurant search/edit, my-orders search/filter)

test_credentials: Admin admin@jivdani.com / Jivdani@2026 (verified). Test restaurants created dynamically with TEST_PL_ / UI_PL_ / UI_MO_ prefix and cleaned via cascade DELETE /api/restaurants/{id}.
seed_data_creation: Backend tests create 2 restaurants per run (test_pl1_{uid}, test_pl2_{uid}@test.com) and 2 orders for a future delivery_date (today+3) to avoid noise with default-tomorrow tests; module fixture cascades cleanup. Frontend test creates 3 restaurants (UI_PL_R1/R2, UI_MO) and 4 orders; cleaned at end via admin DELETE.
context_for_next_testing_agent: JWT token stored in localStorage under key 'jv_token' (NOT 'token'). Restaurant orders route is /my-orders (NOT /restaurant/orders). After restaurant login, default redirect is /order. Purchase-list backend uses UTC tomorrow; frontend's native date input uses local TZ - mostly aligned. backend_test.py + test_iteration2.py together cover all current endpoints. Use REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL from /app/frontend/.env.
